Of calls to privately #> insured patients (reference group), 92.5% resulted in an offered appointment #> (95% Wilson CI: 80.2%-97.7%). Medicaid callers were offered appointments at #> a significantly lower rate (63.8%; 95% CI: 48.3% to 76.9%), representing a #> 28.8 percentage-point absolute deficit and a relative risk of 0.69 #> (Holm-Bonferroni-adjusted p < .001; BCa bootstrap 95% CI for rate #> difference: -36.3 to -18.9 pp). Uninsured callers had the lowest #> appointment-offered rate (55.0%; 95% CI: 39.6% to 69.7%), 37.5 percentage #> points below the privately insured rate (RR 0.60; Holm-adjusted p < .001). #> Medicare callers had a 7.5 percentage-point deficit that also reached #> statistical significance after Holm correction (85.0%; RR 0.92; #> Holm-adjusted p = .037). #> #> Among callers who were offered appointments (n = 119 observations from #> 40 physicians), we analyzed wait time in business days using a Poisson #> generalized linear mixed-effects model with a physician-level random #> intercept to account for within-physician clustering (intraclass correlation #> coefficient 0.073). The Pearson chi-squared overdispersion ratio was 1.12, #> indicating acceptable model fit. Medicaid callers waited 40% longer than #> privately insured callers (IRR 1.40; 95% profile-likelihood CI: 1.12-1.74; #> p = .003). Uninsured callers waited 28% longer (IRR 1.28; 95% CI: 1.01 to 1.62; #> p = .042). No statistically significant wait-time difference was observed for #> Medicare callers compared with privately insured callers (IRR 1.08; 95% CI: #> 0.87-1.35; p = .481).

title: Assembling supplementary digital content
text: mystery-caller study insurance-based access two outcomes — whether appointment offered wait business days among offers — call log carrying caller, call date, practice location. simulate , fit logistic GLMM offer Poisson GLMM wait.
code: set.seed(2026) n <- 150 cities <- list(CO = "Denver", TX = "Dallas", NY = "New York",                CA = "Los Angeles", FL = "Miami", IL = "Chicago") st <- sample(names(cities), n, TRUE) d <- data.frame(   npi        = rep(sprintf("1%09d", seq_len(n)), each = 2),   insurance  = rep(c("Commercial", "Medicaid"), n),   caller     = rep(sample(paste0("RA", 1:5), n, TRUE), each = 2),   call_date  = rep(as.Date("2026-01-05") + sample(0:40, n, TRUE), each = 2),   state      = rep(st, each = 2),   city       = rep(unlist(cities)[st], each = 2),   area       = rep(sample(c("Metro", "Nonmetro"), n, TRUE), each = 2),   degree     = rep(sample(c("MD", "DO"), n, TRUE, c(.8, .2)), each = 2) ) med <- d$insurance == "Medicaid" d$reached <- rbinom(nrow(d), 1, 0.92) == 1   # some calls never reached a live office d$appt_offered <- rbinom(nrow(d), 1, plogis(1.1 - 0.9 * med + 0.3 * (d$area == "Metro"))) # a few calls never resolved the wait (incomplete) -> missing outcome d$wait_days <- ifelse(d$appt_offered == 1 & rbinom(nrow(d), 1, 0.9) == 1,                       rpois(nrow(d), ifelse(med, 18, 12)), NA)  offer_crude    <- mysterycall_logistic_model(d, "appt_offered", "insurance", "npi") offer_adjusted <- mysterycall_logistic_model(d, "appt_offered",                                              c("insurance", "area"), "npi") wait_model <- mysterycall_poisson_model(   d[d$appt_offered == 1 & !is.na(d$wait_days), ], outcome = "wait_days",   predictors = "insurance", random_intercept = "npi")

title: Generating Publication Tables
text: Parameter details: covariates — character vector column names appear row groups table. function detects whether variable continuous (numeric integer > 5 unique values) categorical (factor character, numeric ≤ 5 unique values) formats accordingly. stratify_by — column whose unique values become stratification columns. Pass NULL generate unstratified table single “Overall” column. include_overall — TRUE, column labelled “Overall” prepended stratification columns, showing counts percentages across full sample regardless stratum. cont_stats — controls continuous variables (e.g., wait_days) summarized: * "mean_sd": Mean ± SD, appropriate distribution approximately normal. * "median_iqr": Median [IQR], appropriate right-skewed variables like wait times. * c("mean_sd", "median_iqr"): rows printed. Useful supplements data-quality tables rarely appropriate primary manuscript table. p_value — TRUE, column p-values appended. categorical variables, function runs Pearson chi-squared test; expected cell count min_cell, switches Fisher’s exact test. continuous variables, runs Kruskal-Wallis test (regardless whether cont_stats "mean_sd" "median_iqr") mystery-caller data rarely satisfy normality assumptions required standard t-test ANOVA. Interpreting p-values context: mystery-caller study, p-values Table 1 test whether sampling balanced insurance type. test primary hypothesis (appointment disparity). significant p-value Table 1 means providers assigned Medicaid private-insurance call scenarios differ characteristic, relevant split done something mysterycall_split_and_save(). split random (), Table 1 p-values non-significant. variable_labels — named character vector names column names data values display labels appear table. translate snake_case column names mixed-case, abbreviation-spelled-labels journals require. min_cell — default 5, following standard Fisher’s exact test threshold used biostatistics textbooks. subspecialty comparisons rare specialties (e.g., Reproductive Endocrinology appears < 5% rows), threshold trigger Fisher’s exact test automatically. Note function prints message switches tests:
code: tbl1 <- mysterycall_table1(   data             = analysis_data,   covariates       = c("age_category", "gender_std", "subspecialty",                        "practice_setting", "region_std", "ruca_category"),   stratify_by      = "insurance_type",   include_overall  = TRUE,   cont_stats       = "median_iqr",    # "mean_sd", "median_iqr", or c("mean_sd","median_iqr")   digits           = 1,               # decimal places for percentages   p_value          = TRUE,            # adds chi-sq / Kruskal-Wallis p-value column   min_cell         = 5,               # use Fisher's exact test when expected cell < 5   variable_labels  = c(     age_category     = "Provider age, years",     gender_std       = "Physician sex",     subspecialty     = "Subspecialty",     practice_setting = "Practice setting",     region_std       = "US Census region",     ruca_category    = "Rurality (RUCA category)"   ) )  print(tbl1) # Note: Using Fisher's exact test for 'subspecialty' (minimum expected # cell count = 2.3, below threshold of 5).

title: Generating Publication Tables
text: journals — conference poster sessions — expect significance stars (* p < 0.05; ** p < 0.01; *** p < 0.001) alongside adjusted p-values. Add separate column extracting numeric p-values: Note: journals (including NEJM JAMA) explicitly prohibit significance stars favour exact p-values. Check target journal’s instructions authors adding stars.
code: # Extract numeric p-values (assumes a 'p_numeric' column in the result) disp_tbl$stars <- dplyr::case_when(   disp_tbl$p_numeric < 0.001 ~ "***",   disp_tbl$p_numeric < 0.01  ~ "**",   disp_tbl$p_numeric < 0.05  ~ "*",   TRUE                        ~ "" )  # Combine with formatted p-value for display disp_tbl$p_display <- paste0(   formatC(disp_tbl$p_numeric, format = "f", digits = 3),   disp_tbl$stars )

title: Generating Publication Tables
text: typical output looks like:
code: paragraph <- mysterycall_write_results_paragraph(   model_result    = poisson_model_result,   # output of mysterycall_poisson_model()   disparity_table = disp_tbl,              # output of mysterycall_disparities_table()   outcome_label   = "appointment acceptance",   insurance_var   = "insurance_type",   ref_level       = "Private",   alt_level       = "Medicaid" )  cat(paragraph) Among 1,688 completed calls to 844 unique providers, Medicaid callers were significantly less likely to be offered an appointment than private-insurance callers (59.2% vs. 72.4%; adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 0.61, 95% CI [0.51, 0.73]; p < 0.001). This disparity persisted after adjustment for physician sex, subspecialty, practice setting, US Census region, and rurality (aOR 0.63, 95% CI [0.53, 0.75]; p < 0.001). Among subspecialties, the largest disparity was observed in Urogynecology (aOR 0.44, 95% CI [0.28, 0.70]; p < 0.001) and the smallest in Gynecologic Oncology (aOR 0.81, 95% CI [0.58, 1.13]; p = 0.21).

Mystery-caller protocols carry exclusion vocabulary: wrong number, voicemail, closed system, retired. legitimate. trap vocabularies often quietly include categories outcomes rather exclusions – “accepting new patients”, “requires referral first”, “schedule without records”. refusals. protocol codes exclusions, removed cohort, offer stage loses almost variation. eligible cohort offer rate 100 percent. nothing left model: every office survived exclusion criteria offered appointment, offering one exclusion criterion. Fit logistic model fail converge, converge nothing, natural reading “disparity access” truth question never asked. four “accepting new patients” calls finding. belong denominator.
code: calls <- data.frame(   call_id = sprintf("C%02d", 1:20),   reason  = c(rep("Able to contact", 12),               rep("Not accepting new patients", 4),   # outcome, coded as exclusion               rep("Wrong number listed", 2),          # genuine exclusion               rep("Went to voicemail", 2)),           # genuine exclusion   stringsAsFactors = FALSE ) calls$offered <- calls$reason == "Able to contact"  protocol_eligible <- calls$reason == "Able to contact" all_called        <- rep(TRUE, nrow(calls))  data.frame(   denominator = c("source (everyone called)", "protocol-eligible only"),   n           = c(sum(all_called), sum(protocol_eligible)),   offered     = c(sum(calls$offered[all_called]), sum(calls$offered[protocol_eligible])),   offer_rate  = c(round(100 * mean(calls$offered[all_called]), 1),                   round(100 * mean(calls$offered[protocol_eligible]), 1)) ) #>                denominator  n offered offer_rate #> 1 source (everyone called) 20      12         60 #> 2   protocol-eligible only 12      12        100

title: The Two-Part Model and the Denominator Trap
text: Stated rule: exclusion removes calls question asked; outcome records answer . Wrong number means office never reached, access question posed. “accepting new patients” means office reached said .
code: # Stage 1: offer. Everyone called who could in principle have been offered # something -- genuine unreachables (wrong number, voicemail) removed, refusals # retained, because a refusal is an outcome. genuine_exclusion <- calls$reason %in% c("Wrong number listed", "Went to voicemail") offer_denominator <- !genuine_exclusion  # Stage 2: wait. Offers only. wait_denominator <- calls$offered  data.frame(   stage = c("offer", "wait"),   denominator_n = c(sum(offer_denominator), sum(wait_denominator)),   definition = c("called, minus unreachable-by-construction",                  "appointments offered") ) #>   stage denominator_n                                definition #> 1 offer            16 called, minus unreachable-by-construction #> 2  wait            12                      appointments offered

title: End-to-End Mystery-Caller Workflow Orchestration
text: Mystery-caller wait times measured business days — weekends US federal holidays excluded. mysterycall_count_business_days() counts business days two dates; mysterycall_business_days() applies calculation every row data frame. Business-day wait times computed mysterycall_business_days().
code: # How many business days between a call on a Monday and an appointment on # Friday of the following week?  (Calendar days = 11; business days = 10) bd <- mysterycall_count_business_days(   start_date = "2024-03-04",   # Monday   end_date   = "2024-03-15"    # Friday two weeks later ) cat("Business days:", bd, "\n") #> Business days: 9 # Apply to a data frame of completed calls calls_df <- data.frame(   npi       = paste0("NPI-", 1:6),   insurance = c("Medicaid", "Private", "Medicaid", "Private", "Medicare", "Uninsured"),   call_date = as.Date(c("2024-03-04", "2024-03-04", "2024-03-11",                          "2024-03-11", "2024-03-18", "2024-03-18")),   appt_date = as.Date(c("2024-03-25", "2024-03-12", "2024-04-01",                          "2024-03-19", "2024-03-27", "2024-04-08")) )  # mysterycall_business_days() column params: call_col, appt_col, result_col calls_with_bd <- mysterycall_business_days(   data       = calls_df,   call_col   = "call_date",   appt_col   = "appt_date",   result_col = "wait_days" ) #> Business days computed for 6/6 row(s); stored in column 'wait_days'.  knitr::kable(   calls_with_bd[, c("npi", "insurance", "call_date", "appt_date", "wait_days")],   col.names = c("NPI", "Insurance", "Call date", "Appt date", "Wait (business days)"),   caption   = "Business-day wait times computed by `mysterycall_business_days()`." )

title: End-to-End Mystery-Caller Workflow Orchestration
text: mysterycall_caller_reliability() computes Cohen’s kappa (categorical outcomes) intraclass correlation coefficient (numeric outcomes) records audited two callers.
code: set.seed(7) # Long-format audit sample: each record appears twice — once per caller n_records <- 30L audit_long <- data.frame(   record_id  = rep(1:n_records, 2),   caller     = rep(c("Alice", "Bob"), each = n_records),   appt_offered = c(     sample(c("Yes", "No"), n_records, replace = TRUE, prob = c(0.72, 0.28)),     sample(c("Yes", "No"), n_records, replace = TRUE, prob = c(0.68, 0.32))   ) )  rel <- mysterycall_caller_reliability(   data        = audit_long,   caller_col  = "caller",   outcome_col = "appt_offered",   type        = "kappa" )  print(rel) #> -- mysterycall_caller_reliability -- #> Method       : kappa  #> Statistic    : 0.3478  #> 95% CI       : [ -0.0087 , 0.7043 ] #> N pairs      : 30  #> Interpretation: fair (Landis & Koch)

title: End-to-End Mystery-Caller Workflow Orchestration
text: mysterycall_call_productivity() tallies completed, pending, failed calls caller returns summary data frame QC review. Table: Per-caller productivity mysterycall_call_productivity().
code: set.seed(8) n_rows <- 80L prod_df <- data.frame(   caller           = sample(c("Alice", "Bob", "Carol", "Dana"),                              n_rows, replace = TRUE),   call_date        = sample(seq(as.Date("2024-02-01"), as.Date("2024-03-31"),                                  by = "day"), n_rows, replace = TRUE),   appointment_offered = sample(c(1L, 1L, 1L, 0L), n_rows, replace = TRUE) )  prod <- mysterycall_call_productivity(   data        = prod_df,   caller_col  = "caller",   date_col    = "call_date",   outcome_col = "appointment_offered" )  knitr::kable(   prod$summary,   caption = "Per-caller productivity from `mysterycall_call_productivity()`." )

title: Writing the Results Section
text: Results section access-disparities manuscript restates numbers already live model output tables. Re-typing hand invites whole class bug: sentence says “increasing” coefficient negative, odds ratio 1 described “likely”, confidence interval crosses null written bounded away zero. mysterycall provides family prose builders take estimates emit manuscript-ready sentences whose wording derived sign magnitude data. Wire narrative builders words can never drift step tables. Every builder works plain data frame, vignette needs model fitting — objects returned mysterycall_logistic_model(), mysterycall_poisson_model(), mysterycall_nb_model().

title: Writing the Results Section
text: Two physician subspecialties compared reference group () whether new-patient appointment offered (b) long wait . build estimate tables directly; practice come fitted models’ $or_table / $irr_table elements.
code: # Odds ratios for "appointment offered" (logistic regression output) or_tbl <- data.frame(   term     = c("(Intercept)", "insuranceMedicaid", "insuranceMedicare"),   or       = c(2.10, 0.62, 0.88),   ci_lower = c(1.20, 0.41, 0.63),   ci_upper = c(3.68, 0.94, 1.23),   p_value  = c(0.008, 0.024, 0.451),   stringsAsFactors = FALSE )  # Incidence rate ratios for wait days (Poisson/NB regression output). # `p_value` (numeric) is used by write_results_paragraph(); `p_value_fmt` # (character) is used by irr_to_days() for the in-sentence p-value. irr_tbl <- data.frame(   term        = c("(Intercept)", "insuranceMedicaid", "insuranceMedicare"),   irr         = c(1.00, 1.28, 1.04),   ci_lower    = c(NA,   1.05, 0.90),   ci_upper    = c(NA,   1.56, 1.20),   p_value     = c(NA,   0.014, 0.590),   p_value_fmt = c(NA,   "0.014", "0.590"),   stringsAsFactors = FALSE )

title: Writing the Results Section
text: intro clause claims significance level actually clears alpha; direction (“less likely” / “likely” / “similar odds”) chosen whether sits , , 1.
code: acceptance <- mysterycall_results_paragraph(   or_tbl,   ref_group     = "commercial insurance",   exposure_col  = "insurance",   outcome_label = "a new-patient appointment" ) cat(acceptance) #> Medicaid callers were 38% less likely to be offered a new-patient appointment (OR 0.62, 95% CI 0.41 to 0.94, p=0.024). Medicare callers were 12% less likely to be offered a new-patient appointment (OR 0.88, 95% CI 0.63 to 1.23, p=0.451).

title: Writing the Results Section
code: wait_irr <- mysterycall_write_results_paragraph(   irr_tbl,   ref_group     = "commercial insurance",   exposure_col  = "insurance",   outcome_label = "time to appointment" ) cat(wait_irr) #> In multivariable Poisson regression, insurance was significantly associated with time to appointment (see Table X). Compared with commercial insurance, callers presenting as Medicaid had an IRR of 1.28 (95% CI 1.05 to 1.56; p = 0.014) for time to appointment. Compared with commercial insurance, callers presenting as Medicare had an IRR of 1.04 (95% CI 0.90 to 1.20; p = 0.590) for time to appointment.

what: Translating IRRs to absolute days (signed CIs)
title: Writing the Results Section
text: IRRs hard readers feel. mysterycall_irr_to_days() multiplies reference-group mean wait report absolute day differences — keeps sign confidence interval, flagging interval crosses zero statistically significant. Note Medicare row: day-scale CI spans zero, sentence says rather implying real effect. non-insurance exposure (e.g. subspecialty), drop insurance-specific wording exposure_descriptor = NULL:
code: days <- mysterycall_irr_to_days(   irr_tbl,   baseline_mean = 21,          # mean wait (days) in the reference group   exposure_col  = "insurance",   ref_group     = "commercial insurance" ) cat(days$paragraph) #> Medicaid-insured callers waited a mean of 5.9 more days compared with commercial insurance (95% CI +1.1 to +11.8 days; IRR 1.28; p = 0.014). Medicare-insured callers waited a mean of 0.8 more days compared with commercial insurance (95% CI -2.1 to +4.2 days; IRR 1.04; p = 0.590) (difference not statistically significant). ent_tbl <- data.frame(   term        = c("(Intercept)", "ent_typeLaryngology"),   irr         = c(1.00, 1.20),   ci_lower    = c(NA,   1.02),   ci_upper    = c(NA,   1.41),   p_value_fmt = c(NA,   "0.028"),   stringsAsFactors = FALSE ) ent_days <- mysterycall_irr_to_days(   ent_tbl, baseline_mean = 23, exposure_col = "ent_type",   ref_group = "General", subject = "callers", exposure_descriptor = NULL ) cat(ent_days$sentences[1]) #> Laryngology callers waited a mean of 4.6 more days compared with General (95% CI +0.5 to +9.4 days; IRR 1.20; p = 0.028).

title: Writing the Results Section
text: Straight raw data, model required:
code: set.seed(1) raw <- data.frame(   wait_days = c(rpois(60, 12), rpois(60, 16)),   insurance = rep(c("Private", "Medicaid"), each = 60) ) wt <- mysterycall_wait_time_sentence(   raw, outcome_col = "wait_days", group_col = "insurance",   reference = "Private" ) cat(wt$sentence) #> The median wait time across all insurance was 14 business days (IQR: 12 to 16). Specifically, the median wait time was 15 days (IQR: 13 to 18) for Medicaid, 13 days (IQR: 10 to 15) for Private. The p-value for Medicaid vs Private was < 0.001.

title: Mystery Caller Study Tools for Healthcare Access Research
text: Measuring patient access healthcare requires assembling provider roster, placing calls standardized script, recording wait times refusal rates, modelling disparities insurance type, race, geography. step involves bespoke data-engineering work research teams currently solve ad hoc: custom scripts loop around NPI API’s 1,200-record cap, manual regular expressions parse name fields, silent dplyr::left_join() calls multiply rows lookup table duplicates, hand-crafted Poisson models lack overdispersion diagnostics. mysterycall consolidates work single, tested, documented pipeline. provides taxonomy-based NPI search bypasses record cap, NANP phone validation state-geography checks, physician name parsing credential surname disambiguation, safe join wrappers enforce coverage uniqueness guarantees, Poisson mixed-effects modelling IRR reporting, publication-ready table export (drive-time isochrones mapping available companion mysterymaps package). target users clinical researchers health-services researchers conduct mystery-caller audit studies need reproducible, auditable workflows rather one-scripts.

title: Mystery Caller Study Tools for Healthcare Access Research
text: typical mystery caller study builds provider roster, analyzes call outcomes: Geocoding, drive-time isochrones, mapping now live companion mysterymaps package (mysterymaps::mysterymaps_geocode(), mysterymaps::mysterymaps_isochrones_for_df(), mysterymaps::mysterymaps_map_base()). mysterycall focuses mystery-caller study design, analysis, manuscript outputs.
code: library(mysterycall) library(dplyr)  # ── 1. Build a provider roster ────────────────────────────────────────────────  # Search by taxonomy across all 50 states (bypasses the 1,200-record API cap) all_states <- c(   "AL","AK","AZ","AR","CA","CO","CT","DE","FL","GA","HI","ID","IL","IN",   "IA","KS","KY","LA","ME","MD","MA","MI","MN","MS","MO","MT","NE","NV",   "NH","NJ","NM","NY","NC","ND","OH","OK","OR","PA","RI","SC","SD","TN",   "TX","UT","VT","VA","WA","WV","WI","WY" )  gyn_onc <- mysterycall_search_taxonomy("Gynecologic Oncology", states = all_states)  # Validate NPI numbers before downstream lookups gyn_onc_valid <- mysterycall_validate_npi(gyn_onc)  # Enrich with CMS Physician Compare demographics gyn_onc_enriched <- mysterycall_get_clinician_data(gyn_onc_valid)  # ── 2. Analyze acceptance and wait-time disparities ───────────────────────────  # `calls` is your completed call log: one row per call to a provider in the # roster above, with an `insurance` arm and recorded outcomes/wait times.  # Medicaid vs. private acceptance rate with Wilson CIs and a gap sentence rates <- mysterycall_acceptance_rate_calc(calls, insurance_col = "insurance") print(rates)  # Wait-time model: incidence rate ratios by insurance, clustered by practice fit <- mysterycall_poisson_model(   calls,   outcome = "business_days_until_appointment",   predictors = "insurance",   random_intercept = "practice" ) mysterycall_irr_plot(fit)

title: Area Deprivation Index (ADI) by ZCTA — adi_zcta
text: National Area Deprivation Index every US ZIP Code Tabulation Area (ZCTA), computed American Community Survey (ACS) 5-year estimates sociome (sociome::get_adi()), reproduces Singh ADI via Kolak et al. three-factor decomposition. keyed ZCTA (corresponds closely mailing ZIP), joins physician's practice ZIP directly, without tract crosswalk.

title: Area Deprivation Index (ADI) by ZCTA — adi_zcta
text: data frame 33,800 rows 6 columns: zcta Five-digit ZIP Code Tabulation Area, character string (leading zeros preserved). adi National linear Area Deprivation Index; higher = deprived, roughly mean 100 / SD 20. NA ACS inputs suppressed. adi_financial_strength Financial Strength factor score (one three Kolak et al. ADI sub-domains). adi_economic_hardship Economic Hardship Inequality factor score. adi_education Educational Attainment factor score. year ACS 5-year vintage end year (2022 = 2018-2022).

title: Area Deprivation Index (ADI) by ZCTA — adi_zcta
text: American Community Survey 5-year estimates (US Census Bureau), summarised Area Deprivation Index Singh (2003) implemented sociome: Kolak, Bhatt, Park, Padron & Molefe (2020), "Quantification Neighborhood-Level Social Determinants Health Continental United States," JAMA Network Open 3(1):e1919928.

title: Area Deprivation Index (ADI) by ZCTA — adi_zcta
text: index national relative: higher values indicate greater neighbourhood socioeconomic deprivation. sociome scales linear ADI approximately mean 100 / standard deviation 20 across areas supplied (, US ZCTAs). Roughly 3% ZCTAs NA ADI ACS suppressed one input variables area. Regenerate data-raw/adi_zcta.R (requires Census API key CENSUS_API_KEY). Advancing ACS vintage ZCTA set change relative scaling, ADI values comparable within single build.

title: Internal: perform all cleaning steps common to both exported functions — .mc_clean_core
text: data data frame raw mystery-caller records (e.g. REDCap export).  Must data.frame subclass thereof. id_col Character scalar.  Column used identify unique physicians deduplication (first occurrence kept).  Set NULL skip deduplication. Default "phone". age_col Character scalar NULL.  Name numeric age column. NULL, age processing skipped entirely.  Default "age". age_breaks Numeric vector cut points passed base::cut(). Default c(-Inf, 50, 60, 70, Inf). age_labels Character vector category labels, length length(age_breaks) - 1. Default c("<50 yrs", "50-59 yrs", "60-69 yrs", ">=70 yrs"). wait_col Character scalar NULL.  Wait-time column (business days). Renamed "Business days appointment" output. Default "business_days_until_appointment". insurance_col Character scalar NULL. Default "insurance". Renamed "Insurance" output. gender_col Character scalar NULL. Default "gender". Renamed "Gender" output. credential_col Character scalar NULL. Column holding raw NPPES credential strings ("MD", "", etc.).  Default "Provider.Credential.Text". Renamed "Physician credential" output. academic_col Character scalar NULL. Default "academic_affiliation". Renamed "Academic affiliation" output. rurality_col Character scalar NULL. CBSA type column. Default "cbsatype10". Renamed "Rurality" output. central_col Character scalar NULL. Central-scheduling indicator column. Default "central_number_e_g_appointment_center". Renamed "Central scheduling" output. transfers_col Character scalar NULL. Number--transfers column.  recode applied; column kept -. Default NULL (skip). recode_credential Named character vector mapping raw credential values display labels. Default c("MD" = "Allopathic training", "" = "Osteopathic training"). recode_academic Named character vector mapping raw academic-affiliation values. Default c("University" = "Academic Practice"). recode_rurality Named character vector mapping raw CBSA-type values. Default c("Metro" = "Metropolitan area", "Micro" = "Rural area"). recode_central Named character vector mapping raw central-scheduling values. Default c("Yes" = "Yes, central scheduling"). drop_pii Logical.  TRUE (default), columns named first, last, middle, phone, address, notes, record_id, npi, zip (case-insensitive) removed output. fill_cols Character vector column names forward-fill (last-observation-carried-forward) recoding renaming. Uses tidyr::fill() package installed, zoo::na.locf(), pure-base-R loop. Columns absent data silently ignored. Default c("academic_affiliation", "cbsatype10"). keep_all Logical. TRUE, full column set (minus PII) returned.  FALSE, set standardized columns defined *_col parameters returned.

text: Adds hospital/insurer market-concentration covariate mystery-caller office data, using Kaiser Family Foundation (KFF) published per-MSA Herfindahl-Hirschman Index (HHI). Market consolidation plausible confounder insurance-based access: highly concentrated market dominant system latitude steer scheduling payer. HHI ranges 0-10000 (sum squared percent market shares). Department Justice / Federal Trade Commission Horizontal Merger Guidelines classify markets un-concentrated (< 1000), moderately concentrated (1000-1800), highly concentrated (> 1800); cut-points define hhi_cat. title: Distil key abstract numbers from fitted model objects — mysterycall_abstract_numbers
text: logistic_fit mysterycall_logistic_model object returned mysterycall_logistic_model(), NULL. Provides N, , CI, p-value primary binary outcome (appointment offered). poisson_fit mysterycall_poisson_model mysterycall_nb_model object, NULL. Provides N, IRR, CI, p-value wait time. lmm_fit mysterycall_lmm object returned mysterycall_lmm(), NULL. Provides N, beta coefficient, CI, p-value continuous wait time. LMM log-transformed ($log_transformed == TRUE), beta log-days scale unit label reflects . exposure_term Character scalar. exact term name extract model coefficient table (e.g. "insuranceMedicaid"). Must match term column or_table, irr_table, coef_table exactly. ref_label Character scalar. Human-readable reference group label used abstract sentence (e.g. "commercial insurance"). Default "reference group". comparison_label Character scalar NULL. Human-readable label comparison group (e.g. "Medicaid"). NULL (default), derived exposure_term stripping leading run lowercase letters (e.g. "insuranceMedicaid" becomes "Medicaid"). outcome_label Character scalar. Human-readable outcome description used abstract sentence. Default "appointment acceptance". digits_or Integer. Decimal places , IRR, beta coefficients. Default 2L. digits_p Integer. Decimal places p-values. Default 3L. acceptance_rate Named numeric vector length 2, NULL. form c(ref = 0.82, comparison = 0.61) provide raw acceptance rates reference comparison groups. Used compute absolute percentage-point gap. NULL (default), gap omitted sentence.

title: Distil key abstract numbers from fitted model objects — mysterycall_abstract_numbers
text: list class mysterycall_abstract_numbers elements: n_total integer. Total calls first non-NULL fit (logistic_fit, poisson_fit, lmm_fit). numeric. Odds ratio, NA_real_ logistic_fit NULL exposure_term found. or_ci character. Formatted "0.62 (0.41-0.94)", NA. or_p character. Formatted p-value (e.g. "0.024" "< 0.001"), NA. irr numeric. Incidence rate ratio, NA_real_. irr_ci character NA. irr_p character NA. beta numeric. LMM fixed-effect coefficient (days log-days), NA_real_. beta_ci character NA. beta_p character NA. absolute_gap numeric. ref_rate - comparison_rate proportion units, NA_real_ acceptance_rate NULL. abstract_sentence character. title: Distil key abstract numbers from fitted model objects — mysterycall_abstract_numbers
text: sentence assembled available components order: Lead: "Among [N] total calls, ". clause (logistic_fit non-NULL): primary clause. IRR clause (poisson_fit non-NULL): primary clause present; otherwise appended semicolon. LMM beta clause (lmm_fit non-NULL): primary clause IRR present; otherwise appended semicolon. Absolute gap suffix (acceptance_rate non-NULL): appended ", absolute [outcome_label] gap [X] percentage points ([ref]% vs. [comparison]%)".

title: Distil key abstract numbers from fitted model objects — mysterycall_abstract_numbers
code: # --- Minimal example: logistic fit only ------------------------------------- fake_logistic <- structure(   list(     n        = 412L,     or_table = data.frame(       term     = c("(Intercept)", "insuranceMedicaid"),       or       = c(2.10, 0.62),       ci_lower = c(1.20, 0.41),       ci_upper = c(3.68, 0.94),       p_value  = c(0.008, 0.024),       stringsAsFactors = FALSE     )   ),   class = "mysterycall_logistic_model" )  result <- mysterycall_abstract_numbers(   logistic_fit     = fake_logistic,   exposure_term    = "insuranceMedicaid",   ref_label        = "commercial insurance",   comparison_label = "Medicaid",   acceptance_rate  = c(ref = 0.82, comparison = 0.61) ) print(result) #> mysterycall_abstract_numbers #>  #>   n_total                   412 #>   OR                        0.62 #>   OR_CI                     0.41-0.94 #>   OR_full                   0.62 (0.41 to 0.94) #>   OR_p                      0.024 #>   absolute_gap_pct          21% #>   ref_rate_pct              82% #>   comparison_rate_pct       61% #>   abstract_sentence         #>     Among 412 total calls, Medicaid callers were 38% less likely to be #>     offered appointment acceptance than commercial insurance callers #>     (OR 0.62, 95% CI 0.41-0.94, p = 0.024), with an absolute #>     appointment acceptance gap of 21 percentage points (82% vs. 61%). #>  result$abstract_sentence #> [1] "Among 412 total calls, Medicaid callers were 38% less likely to be offered appointment acceptance than commercial insurance callers (OR 0.62, 95% CI 0.41-0.94, p = 0.024), with an absolute appointment acceptance gap of 21 percentage points (82% vs. 61%)."  # --- Extended example: logistic + Poisson fit ------------------------------- fake_poisson <- structure(   list(     n         = 298L,     irr_table = data.frame(       term      = c("(Intercept)", "insuranceMedicaid"),       irr       = c(0.95, 1.40),       ci_lower  = c(0.70, 1.12),       ci_upper  = c(1.29, 1.75),       p_value   = c(0.782, 0.003),       stringsAsFactors = FALSE     )   ),   class = "mysterycall_poisson_model" )  result2 <- mysterycall_abstract_numbers(   logistic_fit  = fake_logistic,   poisson_fit   = fake_poisson,   exposure_term = "insuranceMedicaid",   ref_label     = "commercial insurance",   acceptance_rate = c(ref = 0.82, comparison = 0.61) ) result2$abstract_sentence #> [1] "Among 412 total calls, Medicaid callers were 38% less likely to be offered appointment acceptance than commercial insurance callers (OR 0.62, 95% CI 0.41-0.94, p = 0.024); wait times were 40% longer (IRR 1.40, 95% CI 1.12-1.75, p = 0.003), with an absolute appointment acceptance gap of 21 percentage points (82% vs. 61%)."

NULL one group evaluated. columns table. sentences Character vector, one entry per insurance group, e.g. "Medicaid acceptance rate: 209/371 = 56.3% (95% CI: 51.2%-61.4%)". gap_sentence Character scalar describing spread.  exactly two groups evaluated: "Physicians accepted Medicaid 56.3% vs BCBS 82.4%, gap 26.1 percentage points." three groups evaluated, sentence reports min--max range. title: Simulation power for a covariate-adjusted NB GLMM with a cluster ICC — mysterycall_adjusted_power
text: existing power tools cluster physician (paired calls). geographic access study instead adjusts confounders clusters callers within higher-level unit – states, markets – whose correlation expressed intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC), random-slope design. Analysts usually paper "+20% clustering" rule thumb. instead simulates power actual adjusted analysis: negative-binomial GLMM wait outcome rural (exposure) fixed effect, subspecialty fixed effect, configurable number nuisance adjustment covariates, state-level random intercept whose SD derived target ICC via sigma = sqrt(ICC/(1 - ICC) * (trigamma(1/phi) + pi^2/3)) – latent-scale decomposition mysterycall_icc() uses. reports power detect rural effect along mean estimated effect, standard error, model convergence rate.

Default 0.05. n_states Number clusters (random-intercept levels). Default 51. n_subspecs Number subspecialty fixed-effect levels (1 drops term). Default 7. n_extra_covars Number nuisance adjustment covariates. Default 6. alpha Two-sided significance level. Default 0.05. n_sim Number Monte Carlo replicates. Default 100. seed Optional integer seed reproducibility. Default NULL.

what: Automatically select and compare wait-time models — mysterycall_auto_model
title: Automatically select and compare wait-time models — mysterycall_auto_model
text: Fits Poisson GLMM first, checks overdispersion, upgrades negative binomial GLMM warranted. Optionally fits Linear Mixed Model (LMM) parallel evaluates whether defensible communication/sensitivity tool. Returns statistically preferred count model structured recommendation attached.

title: Automatically select and compare wait-time models — mysterycall_auto_model
code: mysterycall_auto_model(   data,   outcome,   predictors,   random_intercept,   phi_threshold = mysterycall_overdispersion_threshold(),   conf_level = 0.95,   include_lmm = TRUE,   lmm_normality_threshold = 0.05,   ... )

title: Automatically select and compare wait-time models — mysterycall_auto_model
text: data data frame. outcome Character scalar. Name count (wait-day) outcome column. predictors Character vector fixed-effect column names. random_intercept Character scalar. Grouping column physician random intercept. phi_threshold Numeric. Pearson phi NB model replaces Poisson. Default mysterycall_overdispersion_threshold() (1.5), package-wide overdispersion threshold. conf_level Numeric. Confidence level Wald CIs. Default 0.95. include_lmm Logical. Fit LMM evaluate suitability? Default TRUE. LMM never primary model; always secondary communication/sensitivity check. lmm_normality_threshold Numeric. Shapiro-Wilk p-value threshold LMM residuals considered approximately normal. Default 0.05. ... Additional arguments forwarded model-fitting functions.

title: Automatically select and compare wait-time models — mysterycall_auto_model
text: selected count model - either mysterycall_poisson_model mysterycall_nb_model - extra element $selection: poisson_phi Numeric. Overdispersion initial Poisson fit. model_chosen Character. "poisson" "negative_binomial". reason Character. Explanation count-model selection. lmm mysterycall_lmm object, NULL include_lmm = FALSE fitting failed. lmm_shapiro_p Numeric. Shapiro-Wilk p-value LMM residuals, NA. lmm_defensible Logical. TRUE LMM residuals pass normality outcome range exceeds 30 days. lmm_recommendation Character. Plain-language guidance whether use LMM. recommendation Character. Overall one-paragraph guidance covering primary model LMM.

title: Automatically select and compare wait-time models — mysterycall_auto_model
text: Decision tree Fit Poisson GLMM compute Pearson overdispersion (phi). phi <= phi_threshold: primary model = Poisson. Otherwise: re-fit negative binomial (NB) GLMM. include_lmm = TRUE: fit LMM run Shapiro-Wilk normality test residuals. residuals approximately normal (p >= lmm_normality_threshold) outcome range exceeds 30 days, LMM flagged defensible reporting day-scale coefficients alongside primary count model. Otherwise LMM flagged recommended. primary return value selected count model (Poisson NB) class mysterycall_poisson_model() / mysterycall_nb_model(), downstream functions work unchanged. LMM routing metadata live result$selection.

title: Automatically select and compare wait-time models — mysterycall_auto_model
code: set.seed(1978) df <- data.frame(   wait = rpois(60, 18),   ins  = rep(c("Medicaid", "BCBS"), 30),   phys = rep(paste0("Dr_", 1:10), each = 6),   stringsAsFactors = FALSE ) result <- mysterycall_auto_model(df, "wait", "ins", "phys") #> Step 1/3: Fitting Poisson GLMM to assess overdispersion... #> Fitting Poisson GLMER: wait ~ ins + (1 | phys) #> boundary (singular) fit: see help('isSingular') #> Convergence issues detected: #>   boundary (singular) fit: see help('isSingular') #> Consider simplifying predictors or using nAGQ = 1. #> Singular fit: random-intercept variance is ~0. The physician-level random effect explains little variation. #> Model fitted: n=60, physicians=10, AIC=340.4, overdispersion=0.86 #> Poisson GLMM selected: phi = 0.86 <= 1.5 (no overdispersion detected).  #> Step 3/3: Fitting LMM to evaluate day-scale coefficients... #> Fitting LMM: wait ~ ins + (1 | phys) #> boundary (singular) fit: see help('isSingular') #> Model fitted: n=60, physicians=10, AIC=342.6, sigma=3.93, R2m=0.095, R2c=0.095 print(result) #> Poisson GLMER  n = 60  physicians = 10  AIC = 340.4  BIC = 346.7 #>   Warning: convergence warnings; singular fit #>   Reference levels: ins='BCBS' #>  #> Fixed effects (IRR with Wald CI): #>          term    irr ci_lower ci_upper p_value_fmt #> 1 (Intercept) 17.000   15.587   18.541     < 0.001 #> 2 insMedicaid  1.149    1.020    1.294       0.022 #>  #> Random intercept (phys):  variance = 0.0000  SD = 0.0000 #>  #> === Auto-Model Selection === #> Count model: poisson (Poisson phi = 0.86) #> LMM: Shapiro-Wilk p = 0.830  |  Defensible: NO #>  #> --- Recommendation --- #> PRIMARY MODEL: Poisson GLMM (phi = 0.86 <= 1.5; no overdispersion). Report #>   incidence rate ratios (IRRs) with 95% Wald CIs. SENSITIVITY / #>   COMMUNICATION: LMM is not recommended: outcome range = 17 days (< 30). A #>   floor effect near zero violates the normality assumption. Stick with the #>   Poisson GLMM. Do not report LMM coefficients as primary results. #>

title: Build a propensity-score-matched control cohort — mysterycall_build_matched_controls
text: Many mystery-caller audits case-control design: treated group (private-equity-owned practices, hospital-acquired practices, specific chain) compared otherwise-similar controls. make comparison fair – keep call burden bounded – match treated practice nearby, comparable control. builds matched cohort: fits propensity model treated units versus candidate pool, greedily matches treated unit 1:1 nearest control propensity score, within exact stratum (e.g. state) optional geographic caliper, without replacement.

title: Build a propensity-score-matched control cohort — mysterycall_build_matched_controls
code: mysterycall_build_matched_controls(   treated,   candidates,   ps_formula,   id_col,   exact = NULL,   coords = NULL,   caliper_miles = 10,   min_in_caliper = 1L,   cluster_col = NULL,   seed = 42 )

title: Build a propensity-score-matched control cohort — mysterycall_build_matched_controls
text: treated Data frame treated units (one row per unit, unless cluster_col set). candidates Data frame candidate controls. Must contain propensity covariates, id_col, exact columns, (used) coords columns. ps_formula two-sided formula treatment ~ x1 + x2 + .... left-hand side names treatment indicator function creates internally (1 treated, 0 candidates); right-hand side matching covariates, must exist frames. id_col Name unique identifier column (present frames). exact Optional character vector columns control must match treated unit exactly (e.g. "state"). Default NULL. coords Optional length-2 character vector naming latitude longitude columns (frames), used distance caliper. NULL disables caliper. See mysterycall_geocode_city_state() populate . caliper_miles Maximum control distance miles (haversine). Ignored coords NULL. Default 10. min_in_caliper Require least many candidates within caliper treated unit matched (guards matching isolated control). Default 1. cluster_col Optional column identifying clusters (e.g. office/site shared several treated providers). set, one treated unit per cluster matched; units within cluster tried random order one matches. seed Integer seed within-cluster shuffle (reproducibility). Default 42.

title: Build a propensity-score-matched control cohort — mysterycall_build_matched_controls
text: object class "mysterycall_matched_controls": list pairs (tibble: pair_id, treated_id, control_id, ps_treated, ps_control, ps_diff, distance_miles), matched_treated, matched_controls (matched rows input), ps_model (fitted glm), balance (standardized mean differences numeric covariates, treated vs matched controls), counts n_treated, n_matched, n_unmatched. .data.frame() returns pairs.

title: Build a propensity-score-matched control cohort — mysterycall_build_matched_controls
text: greedy nearest-neighbour scheme one audit teams actually use control must callable (state, short drive away), -- shelf matchers express directly. unconstrained statistical matching consider MatchIt package instead.

title: Build a propensity-score-matched control cohort — mysterycall_build_matched_controls
code: set.seed(1) treated <- data.frame(   npi = 1:20, state = sample(c("CO", "TX"), 20, TRUE),   lat = runif(20, 39, 40), lon = runif(20, -105, -104),   years = rpois(20, 12), female = rbinom(20, 1, 0.5)) candidates <- data.frame(   npi = 101:400, state = sample(c("CO", "TX"), 300, TRUE),   lat = runif(300, 39, 40), lon = runif(300, -105, -104),   years = rpois(300, 10), female = rbinom(300, 1, 0.5)) m <- mysterycall_build_matched_controls(   treated, candidates, treatment ~ years + female,   id_col = "npi", exact = "state", coords = c("lat", "lon"),   caliper_miles = 40) m #> <mysterycall matched controls: 20 of 20 treated matched (0 unmatched)> #>   median control distance: 20.4 miles; max ps difference: 0.077 #>  #> Covariate balance (standardized mean differences): #> # A tibble: 2 × 4 #>   covariate mean_treated mean_control    smd #>   <chr>            <dbl>        <dbl>  <dbl> #> 1 years             11.8         11.8 0.0315 #> 2 female             0.4          0.4 0

code: set.seed(42) df <- data.frame(   wait_days     = round(rnorm(60, 21, 8)),   business_days = round(rnorm(60, 15, 6)),   scenario      = rep(c("Straight", "Lesbian", "Single"), 20),   practice      = rep(paste0("P", 1:20), each = 3),   stringsAsFactors = FALSE ) res <- mysterycall_calendar_sensitivity(   df,   calendar_col     = "wait_days",   business_col     = "business_days",   predictors       = "scenario",   random_intercept = "practice",   ref_label        = "Straight couple",   supp_table_num   = "S2" ) #> Fitting calendar-days model (wait_days)... #> Fitting business-days model (business_days)... #> Warning: Outcome range is only 26 days (< 30). LMM assumes approximate normality; with a narrow range the distribution may be non-normal or floor-censored. Consider Poisson/NB GLMM instead and check the Q-Q plot. #> Warning: Convergence issues detected: #>   boundary (singular) fit: see help('isSingular') #> Warning: Singular fit: physician random-intercept variance is ~0. Consider a fixed-effects-only model. print(res) #> Calendar vs. Business Days Sensitivity Analysis #>   Calendar model: n = 60  |  Business model: n = 60 #>   Direction consistent across all terms: NO -- see Consistent column #>  #>              Term           Calendar days              Business days Consistent #>    scenarioSingle  0 (-6 to 6), p = 1.000 2 (-1.5 to 5.4), p = 0.265        Yes #>  scenarioStraight -1 (-7 to 5), p = 0.736 2 (-1.5 to 5.5), p = 0.253         No #>  #> -- Supplemental paragraph -- #> As a pre-specified sensitivity analysis, we repeated the secondary wait-time #> analysis substituting business days (Monday through Friday, excluding the 11 #> U.S. federal holidays) for calendar days. Business days were computed using the #> R package \emph{bizdays} with a US Federal holiday calendar. The calendar-day #> model included 60 observations with a recorded appointment date; the #> business-day model included 60 observations. Both models used the same #> mixed-effects linear regression specification (scenario as fixed effect #> compared with Straight couple (reference); physician practice as random #> intercept). Results were directionally consistent for most comparisons, with #> the exception of scenarioStraight. Shapiro-Wilk normality tests on model #> residuals: calendar-day model: W = 0.971, p = 0.168; business-day model: W = #> 0.981, p = 0.464. Full results are presented in Supplemental Table S2.

code: mysterycall_caller_drift(   data,   outcome_col = "offered",   date_col = NULL,   call_seq_col = NULL,   caller_col = NULL,   week_or_day = c("week", "day"),   plot = TRUE,   test = c("lm") )

title: Detect and visualise calendar and sequence drift in mystery-caller outcomes — mysterycall_caller_drift
text: data data frame. outcome_col Character scalar. Binary 0/1 outcome column. Default "offered". date_col Character scalar NULL. Date column used detect calendar drift. Default NULL. call_seq_col Character scalar NULL. Integer column giving sequential call number caller (1st call, 2nd call, etc.). Default NULL. NULL date_col caller_col provided, sequence derived ranking dates within caller (ties broken row order). caller_col Character scalar NULL. Grouping column caller identity, used derive call_seq_col argument NULL. Default NULL. week_or_day Character scalar. Aggregation unit calendar trend: "week" (default) "day". plot Logical. TRUE (default) ggplot2 installed, $plot return value ggplot object; otherwise $plot NULL. test Character scalar. Trend-test method. Currently "lm" (default) supported.

title: Detect and visualise calendar and sequence drift in mystery-caller outcomes — mysterycall_caller_drift
text: named list class mysterycall_caller_drift: calendar Named list NULL (date_col NULL). Elements: rate_by_period (data frame columns period, time_index, rate, n), slope, slope_se, p_value, p_fmt, sentence. sequence Named list NULL (sequence information available). Elements: rate_by_seq (data frame columns seq_bin, mean_seq, rate, n), slope, slope_se, p_value, p_fmt, sentence. plot ggplot object NULL. sentence Character scalar. Combined one-sentence summary ready paste methods section, e.g. "Acceptance rates change significantly study period (slope=-0.002 per week, p=0.43) call sequence (slope=0.001 per call, p=0.81), supporting design validity."

title: Detect and visualise calendar and sequence drift in mystery-caller outcomes — mysterycall_caller_drift
text: Calendar drift. outcome_col aggregated week_or_day period. linear model lm(rate \~ time_index) fitted, time_index chronological rank period (1, 2, 3, ...). slope estimated change acceptance rate per week (day). Week boundaries follow format(date, "%Y-%U") (Sunday-start ISO-adjacent convention). Sequence drift. Calls grouped consecutive bins five call_seq_col (within-caller date rank call_seq_col NULL). Within bin acceptance rate mean sequence number computed. linear model lm(rate \~ mean_seq) fitted; slope estimated change acceptance rate per additional call. Significance assessed \(\alpha = 0.05\).

title: Detect and visualise calendar and sequence drift in mystery-caller outcomes — mysterycall_caller_drift
code: set.seed(42) n <- 120L df <- data.frame(   call_date = seq(as.Date("2023-01-02"), by = "day", length.out = n),   caller    = rep(c("Alice", "Bob", "Carol"), times = n / 3L),   offered   = rbinom(n, 1L, 0.55) )  # Calendar + sequence drift (sequence derived from date within caller) res <- mysterycall_caller_drift(   df,   outcome_col = "offered",   date_col    = "call_date",   caller_col  = "caller",   week_or_day = "week",   plot        = FALSE ) cat(res$sentence, "\n") #> Acceptance rates did not change significantly over the study period (slope=+0.001 per week, p = 0.905) or over call sequence (slope=+0.002 per call, p = 0.408), supporting design validity.  res$calendar$p_value #> [1] 0.905223 head(res$calendar$rate_by_period) #>    period time_index      rate n #> 1 2023-01          1 0.3333333 6 #> 2 2023-02          2 0.2857143 7 #> 3 2023-03          3 0.5714286 7 #> 4 2023-04          4 0.5714286 7 #> 5 2023-05          5 0.2857143 7 #> 6 2023-06          6 0.5714286 7  # Explicit call_seq_col, no plot df$seq <- ave(seq_len(n), df$caller, FUN = seq_along) res2 <- mysterycall_caller_drift(   df,   outcome_col  = "offered",   call_seq_col = "seq",   plot         = FALSE ) res2$sequence$slope #> [1] 0.002222222

what: Check Normality and Summarize Data — mysterycall_check_normality
title: Check Normality and Summarize Data — mysterycall_check_normality
text: Checks normality variable using Shapiro-Wilk test, returns summary statistics, –crucially–generates manuscript-ready $interpretation sentence identifies count data recommends Poisson regression appropriate.

title: Check Normality and Summarize Data — mysterycall_check_normality
code: mysterycall_check_normality(   data,   variable,   outcome_label = NULL,   group_label = NULL )

title: Check Normality and Summarize Data — mysterycall_check_normality
text: data dataframe containing data. variable string specifying column name variable checked summarized. outcome_label Optional character scalar. Human-readable label outcome used interpretation sentence (e.g., "days appointment"). Defaults variable. group_label Optional character scalar. Human-readable label grouping variable used interpretation sentence (e.g., "insurance type"). Defaults "grouping variable".

title: Check Normality and Summarize Data — mysterycall_check_normality
text: named list containing: is_normal Logical. TRUE Shapiro-Wilk p > 0.05. p_value Numeric. Shapiro-Wilk p-value. w_statistic Numeric. Shapiro-Wilk W statistic. is_count Logical. TRUE non-missing values non-negative integers – heuristic count outcomes. mean, sd Numeric scalars (present is_normal = TRUE). median, iqr Numeric scalars (present is_normal = FALSE). interpretation Character scalar. single manuscript-ready paragraph describing distribution , non-normal count data, recommending Poisson regression t-test Kruskal-Wallis. Side effects: emits histogram + density plot Q-Q plot.

title: Check Normality and Summarize Data — mysterycall_check_normality
text: data normally distributed consist counts (non-negative integers), returned sentence reads: "data normally distributed (Shapiro-Wilk W = X, p = Y). Plus count data. t-test assumes data normally distributed, comparing means count data also appropriate. can check incidence rate ratio (IRR) comparison outcome among categories grouping variable. Better use Poisson regression."

title: Check Normality and Summarize Data — mysterycall_check_normality
code: sample_data <- data.frame(   business_days_until_appointment = c(1L, 3L, 2L, 5L, 0L, 4L, 7L, 2L, 1L, 14L) ) result <- mysterycall_check_normality(   sample_data, "business_days_until_appointment",   outcome_label = "days until appointment",   group_label   = "insurance type" ) #> Normality check for 'business_days_until_appointment': n = 10 #> Not normally distributed. Median = 2.5, IQR = 3.5 [count data -- Poisson recommended] #> The data is not normally distributed (Shapiro-Wilk W = 0.813, p = 0.021). Plus it is count data. t-test assumes that data is normally distributed, and comparing the means of count data is also not appropriate. We can check the incidence rate ratio (IRR) for comparison of days until appointment among the categories of insurance type. Better to use Poisson regression. Median days until appointment: 2.5 (IQR: 3.5). cat(result$interpretation) #> The data is not normally distributed (Shapiro-Wilk W = 0.813, p = 0.021). Plus it is count data. t-test assumes that data is normally distributed, and comparing the means of count data is also not appropriate. title: Test for zero-inflation in a fitted count model — mysterycall_check_zero_inflation
code: set.seed(42) df <- data.frame(   wait = rpois(60, lambda = 15),   ins  = rep(c("Medicaid", "BCBS"), 30),   phys = rep(paste0("Dr", 1:10), each = 6),   stringsAsFactors = FALSE ) fit <- mysterycall_poisson_model(df, "wait", "ins", "phys") #> Fitting Poisson GLMER: wait ~ ins + (1 | phys) #> boundary (singular) fit: see help('isSingular') #> Convergence issues detected: #>   boundary (singular) fit: see help('isSingular') #> Consider simplifying predictors or using nAGQ = 1. #> Singular fit: random-intercept variance is ~0. The physician-level random effect explains little variation. #> Model fitted: n=60, physicians=10, AIC=347.3, overdispersion=1.11 mysterycall_check_zero_inflation(fit, plot = FALSE) #> No zero-inflation detected (p = 1.000).

title: Classify RUCA codes into Urban / Suburban / Rural — mysterycall_classify_ruca
text: 2010-vintage RUCA codes standard crosswalk applied 2023 CMS HRSA analyses. Although newer ACS-based updates exist, 2010 vintage remains widely cited peer-reviewed healthcare access research. RUCA crosswalk bundled package. function recodes numeric ruca_code supply; obtaining crosswalk . ZIP- tract-level files available USDA ERS (https://www.ers.usda.gov/data-products/rural-urban-commuting-area-codes). Join data crosswalk first, pass resulting ruca_code column function. Mind vintage . 2010 RUCA files keyed 2010 ZIP codes 2010 census tracts, whereas geographies produced mysterycall_geocode_address() mysterycall_assign_area_covariates() 2020-vintage. Joining 2020 tract GEOIDs 2010 RUCA tract file silently mismatches wherever tracts split merged censuses. Either use 2020-vintage RUCA file, join ZIP rather tract.

title: Clean raw mystery-caller data for publication-ready analysis — mysterycall_clean_data
text: data data frame raw mystery-caller records (e.g. REDCap export).  Must data.frame subclass thereof. id_col Character scalar.  Column used identify unique physicians deduplication (first occurrence kept).  Set NULL skip deduplication. Default "phone". age_col Character scalar NULL.  Name numeric age column. NULL, age processing skipped entirely.  Default "age". age_breaks Numeric vector cut points passed base::cut(). Default c(-Inf, 50, 60, 70, Inf). age_labels Character vector category labels, length length(age_breaks) - 1. Default c("<50 yrs", "50-59 yrs", "60-69 yrs", ">=70 yrs"). wait_col Character scalar NULL.  Wait-time column (business days). Renamed "Business days appointment" output. Default "business_days_until_appointment". insurance_col Character scalar NULL. Default "insurance". Renamed "Insurance" output. gender_col Character scalar NULL. Default "gender". Renamed "Gender" output. credential_col Character scalar NULL. Column holding raw NPPES credential strings ("MD", "", etc.).  Default "Provider.Credential.Text". Renamed "Physician credential" output. academic_col Character scalar NULL. Default "academic_affiliation". Renamed "Academic affiliation" output. rurality_col Character scalar NULL. CBSA type column. Default "cbsatype10". Renamed "Rurality" output. central_col Character scalar NULL. Central-scheduling indicator column. Default "central_number_e_g_appointment_center". Renamed "Central scheduling" output. transfers_col Character scalar NULL. Number--transfers column.  recode applied; column kept -. Default NULL (skip). recode_credential Named character vector mapping raw credential values display labels. Default c("MD" = "Allopathic training", "" = "Osteopathic training"). recode_academic Named character vector mapping raw academic-affiliation values. Default c("University" = "Academic Practice"). recode_rurality Named character vector mapping raw CBSA-type values. Default c("Metro" = "Metropolitan area", "Micro" = "Rural area"). recode_central Named character vector mapping raw central-scheduling values. Default c("Yes" = "Yes, central scheduling"). drop_pii Logical.  TRUE (default), columns named first, last, middle, phone, address, notes, record_id, npi, zip (case-insensitive) removed output. fill_cols Character vector column names forward-fill (last-observation-carried-forward) recoding renaming. Uses tidyr::fill() package installed, zoo::na.locf(), pure-base-R loop. Columns absent data silently ignored. Default c("academic_affiliation", "cbsatype10").

title: Define a Guideline-Concordance Rubric — mysterycall_concordance_rubric

title: Define a Guideline-Concordance Rubric — mysterycall_concordance_rubric
text: item Character vector. Machine-readable item ids. must match column captured-call data passed mysterycall_score_concordance(). Must unique. label Character vector. Manuscript-facing wording per item. Recycled length(item). Default: item. type Character vector. One "binary", "expected_present", "reference_match", "evidence_tier". Recycled. Default "binary". binary Concordant value equals correct. expected_present Concordant cue elicited (correct forced TRUE). reference_match Concordant value equals per-row reference column named reference_col (gold standard varies scenario / state / date). evidence_tier value set named options per call; concordant includes least one option "concordant" tier tier_lookup. correct Expected value(s) binary items. scalar (recycled), vector length length(item), list. Ignored reference_match evidence_tier. Default TRUE. reference_col Character vector. reference_match items, name per-row gold-standard column. Recycled. Default NA. tier_lookup Data frame NULL. evidence_tier items, table columns option, tier ("concordant" / "nonconcordant" / "neutral") optional effective_from / effective_to dates date-versioned guidelines. Default NULL. weight Numeric vector. Composite-score weights (> 0). Recycled. Default 1. na_policy Character vector. treat uncodable / unreached items: "not_applicable" drops item call's denominator (natural handling within-encounter conversation exits); "incorrect" counts non-concordant full denominator. Recycled. Default "not_applicable". option_sep Character scalar. Delimiter evidence_tier option columns supplied strings. Default ";".

Calls match inclusion_value counted included. row match inclusion_value value exclusion_categories silently classified unrecognised contributes denominator named exclusion bucket.

title: Summarise call-level exclusions into a manuscript-ready paragraph — mysterycall_exclusion_summary
code: ## --- minimal runnable example (base R only) ------------------------------- reasons <- c(   "Able to contact",   "Phone not answered or busy signal on repeat calls",   "Went to voicemail",   "Number contacted did not correspond to expected office/specialty",   "Physician referral required before scheduling appointment",   "Not accepting new patients",   "Greater than 5 minutes on hold" ) n_each <- c(120L, 40L, 30L, 10L, 15L, 20L, 5L)  df <- data.frame(   call_id               = seq_len(sum(n_each)),   reason_for_exclusions = rep(reasons, n_each),   stringsAsFactors      = FALSE )  result <- mysterycall_exclusion_summary(df) print(result)       # prints the prose paragraph #> A total of 240 phone calls were made. Of these, 80 (33.3%) calls were unsuccessful connections, including calls in which the phone was not answered or the caller received a busy signal (n = 40), calls that went to voicemail (n = 30), and calls for which the number reached did not correspond to the expected office or specialty (n = 10). The remaining 160 (66.7%) calls resulted in a successful connection with office staff. Among successfully connected calls, 15 offices required a physician referral before an appointment could be scheduled, 20 offices were not accepting new patients, and 5 calls were placed on hold for more than 5 minutes. After applying all exclusion criteria, 120 (50.0%) calls were included in the final analysis.  result$table        # tabyl-style counts #>             category #> 1           included #> 2 phone_not_answered #> 3          voicemail #> 4       wrong_number #> 5  referral_required #> 6      not_accepting #> 7            on_hold #>                                                              label   n #> 1                                             Included in analysis 120 #> 2                Phone not answered or busy signal on repeat calls  40 #> 3                                                Went to voicemail  30 #> 4 Number contacted did not correspond to expected office/specialty  10 #> 5        Physician referral required before scheduling appointment  15 #> 6                                       Not accepting new patients  20 #> 7                                   Greater than 5 minutes on hold   5 #>         pct #> 1 50.000000 #> 2 16.666667 #> 3 12.500000 #> 4  4.166667 #> 5  6.250000 #> 6  8.333333 #> 7  2.083333  ## --- custom exclusion values (different study coding scheme) -------------- df2 <- df names(df2)[2] <- "call_outcome" result2 <- mysterycall_exclusion_summary(   data          = df2,   exclusion_col = "call_outcome",   inclusion_value = "Able to contact",   exclusion_categories = c(     phone_not_answered = "Phone not answered or busy signal on repeat calls",     voicemail          = "Went to voicemail",     wrong_number       = "Number contacted did not correspond to expected office/specialty",     referral_required  = "Physician referral required before scheduling appointment",     not_accepting      = "Not accepting new patients",     on_hold            = "Greater than 5 minutes on hold"   ) ) cat(result2$paragraph) #> A total of 240 phone calls were made. Of these, 80 (33.3%) calls were unsuccessful connections, including calls in which the phone was not answered or the caller received a busy signal (n = 40), calls that went to voicemail (n = 30), and calls for which the number reached did not correspond to the expected office or specialty (n = 10). The remaining 160 (66.7%) calls resulted in a successful connection with office staff. Among successfully connected calls, 15 offices required a physician referral before an appointment could be scheduled, 20 offices were not accepting new patients, and 5 calls were placed on hold for more than 5 minutes. After applying all exclusion criteria, 120 (50.0%) calls were included in the final analysis.  ## --- deduplicate by provider before counting ------------------------------ df3 <- df df3$npi <- c(   seq_len(120L),                  # included (unique)   rep(121L, 40L),                 # one provider, 40 no-answer attempts   seq_len(sum(n_each[-c(1L, 2L)])) + 121L  # remaining unique providers ) # id_col collapses repeated dials to the same NPI result3 <- mysterycall_exclusion_summary(df3, id_col = "npi") result3$total   # unique providers, not raw call rows #> [1] 201

title: Population-average GEE model for a clustered binary audit outcome — mysterycall_gee
text: companion subject-specific mixed model (mysterycall_logistic_model()). GLMM estimates conditional (within-practice) log-odds needs cluster's random intercept estimable, generalized estimating equation (GEE) estimates population-average (marginal) log-odds treats within-practice correlation nuisance modelled – happily uses every record, including singleton dyad practices matched analysis drop. marginal-versus-conditional contrast standard sensitivity analysis clustered binary access outcomes: agreement sign rough magnitude across two targets inference reassuring, divergence worth sentence paper. Robust ("sandwich") standard errors make result insensitive working-correlation choice.

text: Poisson models: $$\text{ICC} = \frac{\sigma^2_u}{\sigma^2_u + \pi^2/3}$$ negative binomial models: $$\text{ICC} = \frac{\sigma^2_u}{\sigma^2_u + \psi_1(1/\theta) + \pi^2/3}$$ \(\sigma^2_u\) physician random-intercept variance, \(\pi^2/3\) logistic-distribution variance (latent-variable approximation), \(\psi_1\) trigamma function.

text: Rubin's rules (1987) \(\bar{Q} = \frac{1}{m} \sum_{=1}^{m} \hat{\beta}_i\) (pooled estimate) \(\bar{U} = \frac{1}{m} \sum_{=1}^{m} \hat{\text{SE}}_i^2\) (within-imputation variance) \(B = \frac{1}{m-1} \sum_{=1}^{m} (\hat{\beta}_i - \bar{Q})^2\) (-imputation variance) \(T = \bar{U} + \left(1 + \frac{1}{m}\right) B\) (total variance) Degrees freedom: \(\nu = (m-1) \left(1 + \frac{\bar{U}}{(1+1/m) B}\right)^2\) Fraction missing information: \(\text{FMI} = \frac{B + B/m}{T}\)

code: if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ library(lme4)  set.seed(42) df <- data.frame(   wait_days = rpois(120, lambda = 20),   scenario  = rep(c("Urgent", "Routine"), each = 60),   insurance = rep(c("Medicaid", "BCBS", "Medicare"), times = 40),   physician = rep(paste0("Dr", 1:10), each = 12),   stringsAsFactors = FALSE )  fit <- lme4::glmer(   wait_days ~ scenario * insurance + (1 | physician),   data   = df,   family = poisson() )  result <- mysterycall_interaction_sentences(   model         = fit,   var1          = "scenario",   var2          = "insurance",   ref_group2    = "BCBS",   outcome_label = "wait time (days)" )  print(result)          # prints paragraph to console result$sentences       # named vector, one element per scenario level result$emmeans_table   # raw emmeans data frame } # }

code: # Fake a mysterycall_logistic_model object -- no lme4 required. # The LRT refit will be caught by tryCatch (model = NULL) and lrt_p = NA. fake_or_table <- data.frame(   term        = c("(Intercept)",                   "insuranceMedicaid",                   "specialtyGYN",                   "insuranceMedicaid:specialtyGYN",                   "insuranceMedicaid:specialtyOB"),   estimate    = c( 0.80, -0.20,  0.15, -0.45,  0.31),   se          = c( 0.18,  0.14,  0.12,  0.21,  0.19),   z_value     = c( 4.44, -1.43,  1.25, -2.14,  1.63),   p_value     = c( 0.001,  0.153,  0.211,  0.032,  0.103),   p_value_fmt = c("< 0.001", "0.153", "0.211", "0.032", "0.103"),   or          = c( 2.23,  0.82,  1.16,  0.64,  1.36),   ci_lower    = c( 1.56,  0.62,  0.92,  0.42,  0.94),   ci_upper    = c( 3.19,  1.08,  1.46,  0.97,  1.97),   stringsAsFactors = FALSE ) fake_fit <- structure(   list(     model      = NULL,     or_table   = fake_or_table,     n          = 200L,     n_clusters = 40L,     formula    = stats::as.formula(                    "offered ~ insurance * specialty + (1 | physician)"                  )   ),   class = "mysterycall_logistic_model" )  result <- mysterycall_interaction_table(fake_fit, "insurance", "specialty") #> Warning: fit$model is NULL (likely a fake/stub object); LRT p-value set to NA. print(result) #> Interaction table: insurance x specialty  (conf_level = 0.95) #>  #> Stratum-specific odds ratios (OR with CI): #>                            term   or ci_lower ci_upper p-value #>  insuranceMedicaid:specialtyGYN 0.64     0.42     0.97   0.032 #>   insuranceMedicaid:specialtyOB 1.36     0.94     1.97   0.103 #>  #> Omnibus LRT p-value: NA #>  #> The interaction between insurance and specialty was undetermined (LRT could not be computed) (LRT p=NA).

title: Generate a complete Materials & Methods section for a mystery-caller study — mysterycall_materials_methods
code: m <- mysterycall_materials_methods(   callers    = c("Lizeth", "Merilyn", "Jessica"),   irb_number = "COMIRB-2024-001" ) print(m) #> === Materials & Methods Section === #>  #> -- caller standardization -- #> Three female research team members (Jessica, Lizeth, and Merilyn) were trained #> as standardized callers prior to data collection. All callers used an identical #> verbatim call script (see Appendix A); no improvisation was permitted. Callers #> identified themselves as prospective new patients, provided the scripted #> clinical complaint, stated their insurance type when asked, and requested the #> first available appointment offered. Calls were placed during standard business #> hours (Monday through Friday, 9:00 am - 4:00 pm local time). [Inter-caller #> reliability results pending - run mysterycall_caller_reliability()] #>  #>  #> -- call spacing -- #> To minimize scheduler recognition across repeated calls to the same practice, a #> minimum interval of 24 hours elapsed between any two calls to the same #> physician's office. Caller assignment was rotated systematically across #> physicians and conditions to prevent caller-by-condition confounding. #>  #>  #> -- appointment definition -- #> The primary outcome was the number of calendar days from the date of the call #> to the date of the first available appointment offered. Callers recorded the #> appointment date offered but did not confirm or accept any appointment. Calls #> in which no appointment was offered were recorded as unsuccessful and excluded #> from wait-time analyses. #>  #>  #> -- physician selection -- #> Eligible physicians were board-certified Female Pelvic Medicine and #> Reconstructive Surgery (FPMRS) specialists identified through a random sample #> of the patient-facing physician directory (voicesforpfd.org). [N physicians - #> confirm from data]. Physicians were not contacted in advance and were unaware #> of their inclusion in the study. #>  #>  #> -- missing data -- #> [N complete] of [N total] calls ([%]) had a complete appointment date. To #> evaluate whether calls with missing appointment dates differed systematically #> from those with complete data, physician and call characteristics were compared #> between groups (see Supplemental Table [X] for the missing data analysis). #>  #>  #> -- business days -- #> Although business days are the preferred scheduling metric, calendar days were #> used as the primary unit because federal holiday calendars vary by state and #> institution. A sensitivity analysis using business days (excluding weekends and #> U.S. federal holidays) is reported in Supplemental Table [X]. #>  #>  #> -- irb -- #> The study was approved by the Colorado Multiple Institutional Review Board #> (COMIRB) (Protocol No. COMIRB-2024-001). Given that office staff were unaware #> they were being observed, the board granted a waiver of informed consent, #> classifying the study as minimal risk. No protected health information was #> collected, and no actual appointments were scheduled. The verbatim call script #> is reproduced in Appendix A. #>  #>  #> Items requiring manual input: #>   [ ] Inter-caller reliability results (provide caller_col and outcome_col) #>   [ ] N physicians (provide physician_col) #>   [ ] N total calls (provide data) #>   [ ] N complete calls (provide outcome_col) #>   [ ] Supplemental table number for missing data analysis #>   [ ] Supplemental table number for business-days sensitivity analysis

title: Generate a boilerplate methods paragraph for a mystery-caller study — mysterycall_methods_paragraph
code: mysterycall_methods_paragraph(   n_physicians  = 369,   n_cities      = 10,   specialties   = c("otolaryngology", "neurotology"),   insurance_types = c("Medicaid", "Blue Cross Blue Shield") ) #> [1] "A mystery-caller audit methodology was employed. A total of 369 physicians representing otolaryngology and neurotology were identified from publicly available directories across 10 cities and states in the United States. Mystery callers posed as new patients insured with Medicaid and Blue Cross Blue Shield and contacted each physician's office to request the earliest available new-patient appointment. Calls were standardized and completed within one week of each other. The primary outcome was business days until a new-patient appointment. All analyses were performed using R (R Foundation for Statistical Computing). A multilevel Poisson regression model with physician random intercepts was fit using the lme4 package to estimate incidence rate ratios (IRR) for the primary outcomes."  mysterycall_methods_paragraph(   n_physicians    = 216,   n_cities        = 12,   specialties     = "otolaryngology",   model_family    = "negative_binomial" ) #> [1] "A mystery-caller audit methodology was employed. A total of 216 physicians representing otolaryngology were identified from publicly available directories across 12 cities and states in the United States. Mystery callers posed as new patients insured with Medicaid and commercial insurance and contacted each physician's office to request the earliest available new-patient appointment. Calls were standardized and completed within one week of each other. The primary outcome was business days until a new-patient appointment. All analyses were performed using R (R Foundation for Statistical Computing). A multilevel negative binomial regression model with physician random intercepts was fit using the glmmTMB package to account for overdispersion in appointment wait times and estimate incidence rate ratios (IRR)."

Missingness was #> significantly associated with: physician. This pattern is consistent with data #> missing at random (MAR) conditional on observed covariates. title: Simulate power for a negative binomial mixed model — mysterycall_nb_power

title: Simulate power for a negative binomial mixed model — mysterycall_nb_power
text: n_physicians Integer. Number physicians (clusters) per group. calls_per_physician Integer. Number mystery calls per physician. Default 2L (one Medicaid, one reference insurance). irr Numeric. IRR detect (e.g. 0.75 means 25% fewer days intervention group). Must positive. theta Numeric. Negative binomial dispersion parameter. Higher values mean less overdispersion (Poisson limit theta -> Inf). Use $theta pilot mysterycall_nb_model() fit, literature-based estimate. Default 2.0 (moderate overdispersion typical wait-time data). baseline_mean Numeric. Expected mean wait days reference group. Default 21 (three weeks). sigma_u Numeric. Standard deviation physician-level random intercept (log scale). Default 0.3 (typical specialty scheduling). alpha Numeric. Type error rate. Default 0.05. n_sim Integer. Number Monte Carlo simulations. Default 1000L. Use least 500 stable estimates; 2000 publication. seed Integer NULL. Random seed reproducibility. Default 42L.

title: Simulate power for a negative binomial mixed model — mysterycall_nb_power

Number simulations run. ci Numeric vector length 2. 95% Wilson CI around power estimate.

title: Simulate power for a negative binomial mixed model — mysterycall_nb_power
text: pilot data, fit mysterycall_nb_model() use result$theta. Without pilot data, use theta = 1 (high overdispersion, conservative) theta = 5 (mild overdispersion). Smaller theta -> lower power -> larger required N.

title: Test overdispersion in a fitted count model — mysterycall_overdispersion_test
text: mixed-effects models (glmmTMB, merMod), df.residual() counts fixed-effect parameters ignores effective degrees freedom consumed random effects, phi approximation rather exact dispersion ratio. verbal interpretation accounts treating low residual phi expected negative-binomial mixed models (dispersion absorbed NB variance random intercepts) rather overfitting. formal simulation-based check GLMM, prefer DHARMa::testDispersion().

title: Test overdispersion in a fitted count model — mysterycall_overdispersion_test
code: ## Poisson GLM on count data ------------------------------------------------ set.seed(42) n   <- 200 dat <- data.frame(   y   = rpois(n, lambda = exp(0.5 + 0.3 * rnorm(n))),   x1  = rnorm(n),   grp = sample(c("A", "B"), n, replace = TRUE) ) fit <- glm(y ~ x1 + grp, data = dat, family = poisson()) result <- mysterycall_overdispersion_test(fit) print(result) #> Pearson dispersion phi=1.240 (chi-sq=244, df=197, p=0.012): Mild overdispersion (phi=1.240), below the negative-binomial switch threshold.  #> The Poisson model is likely adequate; monitor diagnostics. Switch to mysterycall_nb_model() only if phi reaches the moderate band.   ## Gaussian GLM (non-count, shows underdispersion path) --------------------- fit2 <- glm(mpg ~ wt + cyl, data = mtcars, family = gaussian()) mysterycall_overdispersion_test(fit2) #> Pearson dispersion phi=6.592 (chi-sq=191, df=29, p=< 0.001): Severe overdispersion (phi=6.592). Negative binomial or zero-inflated model strongly recommended.  #> Switch to a negative binomial or zero-inflated negative binomial model immediately; Poisson standard errors are severely underestimated.
