title: Plot disparity metrics from a mysterycall_disparities_table — mysterycall_plot_disparities
text: x mysterycall_disparities_table object returned mysterycall_disparities_table(), plain data frame least columns required chosen metric (see Details). metric Character scalar. disparity metric display x-axis: "rate" (default) Appointment-offered rate group CI. vertical dashed reference line marks reference group rate. "abs_diff" Absolute difference percentage points versus reference group. Reference line 0. "rel_risk" Relative risk versus reference group. Reference line 1. show_ref Logical. TRUE (default) reference group row included plot, drawn color_ref diamond shape. show_p Logical. TRUE (default) formatted p-value annotated right non-reference point. color_sig Character. Color groups whose p_value < 0.05. Default "#C0392B" (red). color_ns Character. Color non-significant groups (p_value absent). Default "#2C3E50" (dark navy). color_ref Character. Color reference group point. Default "#2166AC" (blue). point_size Numeric. Diameter estimate point. Default 3. x_label Character NULL. X-axis label. NULL (default) picks label automatically metric. x_pct Logical. TRUE (default "rate" "abs_diff") x-axis formatted percentage. Ignored metric = "rel_risk". title Character NULL. Plot title. Default NULL (title).

title: Plot disparity metrics from a mysterycall_disparities_table — mysterycall_plot_disparities

title: Plot disparity metrics from a mysterycall_disparities_table — mysterycall_plot_disparities

text: irr Numeric. minimum detectable incidence rate ratio. Must positive equal 1. lambda_ref Numeric. Expected mean wait time (days) reference insurance group (e.g. BCBS). Must positive. alpha Numeric. Two-sided type error rate. Default 0.05. power Numeric. Desired statistical power (1 - beta). Default 0.80. both_arms Logical. TRUE, provider called insurance types (paired design), halving total providers needed. Default TRUE. icc Numeric [0, 1). Intra-cluster correlation providers clustered (e.g. practice). text: named list elements: n_per_arm Providers needed per insurance arm. n_total Total providers needed. n_total_calls Total calls placed (= n_per_arm * 2 n_total * 2 paired design). irr, lambda_ref, lambda_trt Input parameters plus derived treatment-arm mean. alpha, power Input parameters. design_effect Inflation factor icc > 0.

title: Sample-size calculation for a Poisson mystery caller study — mysterycall_poisson_power
text: sample-size formula derived score test comparing two independent Poisson rates \(\lambda_0\) (reference arm, e.g. BCBS) \(\lambda_1 = \text{IRR} \times \lambda_0\) (treatment arm, e.g. Medicaid): $$n = \frac{(z_{\alpha/2} + z_\beta)^2 \left(\frac{1}{\lambda_0} + \frac{1}{\lambda_1}\right)}{(\log \text{IRR})^2}$$ gives providers per arm. Total providers = n * 2. provider called insurance types (both_arms = TRUE), n providers needed total.

text: named list elements: n_simple Unadjusted sample size per group two-proportion \(z\)-test (integer). n_adjusted Clustering-adjusted sample size per group, \(\lceil n_{\text{simple}} \times \text{VIF} \rceil\) (integer). vif Variance inflation factor \(1 + (m - 1)\,\rho\). p1 Input baseline acceptance probability. p2 Input comparison acceptance probability (NULL). alpha Input significance level. power Achieved power returned n_simple. solving n, reflects power ceiling-rounded n_simple \(\geq\) requested power. n supplied directly, back-calculated power. icc Input intraclass correlation. m Input average cluster size. message character string suitable manuscript methods section summarising key design parameters result.

title: Clustered binary power and sample-size calculator (GLMM / VIF approach) — mysterycall_power_calc
text: unadjusted sample size per group (\(n_{\text{simple}}\)) comes standard unpooled two-proportion \(z\)-test: $$n_{\text{simple}} = \frac{(z_{\alpha/2} + z_{\beta})^2   [p_1(1-p_1) + p_2(1-p_2)]}{(p_1 - p_2)^2}$$ clustering adjustment uses variance inflation factor: $$\text{VIF} = 1 + (m - 1)\,\rho$$ \(m\) average cluster size (calls per physician) \(\rho\) intraclass correlation (ICC). adjusted sample size : $$n_{\text{adjusted}} = \lceil n_{\text{simple}} \times \text{VIF} \rceil$$ n supplied instead leaving NULL, function back-calculates achieved power n (treated \(n_{\text{simple}}\), clustering).

title: Reconcile a binary
text: Call logs often record appointment fact twice: coarse binary "appointment offered" flag richer categorical disposition (e.g. "sampled physician", "appointment offered"). drift apart data entry. function finds – optionally fixes – two kinds contradiction:

title: Reconcile a binary
code: mysterycall_reconcile_offer_outcome(   data,   flag_col,   outcome_col,   offered_values,   not_offered_values,   dependent_cols = character(0),   action = c("flag", "fix"),   true_value = c(TRUE, "TRUE"),   false_value = c(FALSE, "FALSE"),   clear_value = NA,   id_col = NULL )

title: Reconcile a binary
text: data data frame one row per call. flag_col Name binary offered flag column. outcome_col Name granular disposition column. offered_values Values outcome_col imply appointment offered. not_offered_values Values outcome_col imply appointment offered. dependent_cols Character vector columns blank row flipped "offered" (e.g. c("wait_days_business", "appointment_date")). Default none. action "flag" (default) detect report discordance without changing data, "fix" apply corrections. true_value, false_value value(s) represent offered / offered flag_col. Matching uses %%, pass every spelling present (defaults cover logical character TRUE/FALSE). action = "fix" first element written back, coerced column's type. clear_value Value written dependent_cols -offered flip. Defaults NA; use "" character columns export na = "". id_col Optional identifier column included discordance report.

title: Reconcile a binary
text: object class "mysterycall_offer_reconciliation": list data (unchanged action = "flag", corrected "fix"), discordant (tibble: row, optional id, flag, outcome, direction, suggested), n_understated / n_overstated counts. .data.frame() returns discordance report.

title: Reconcile a binary
text: flag understates outcome: disposition names appointment offered, flag says . flag set "offered". flag overstates outcome: flag says appointment offered, disposition says none . flag set "offered" dependent_cols (wait time, appointment date) cleared "wait exists appointment offered" invariant holds. granular outcome_col treated authoritative. Rows whose outcome neither offered_values not_offered_values left untouched.

title: Three-tier specialty reconciliation with audit columns — mysterycall_reconcile_specialty
text: Applies three-tier decision rule: Tier 1 (high): primary column non-missing non-default - use -. Tier 2 (medium): primary missing default label, secondary column informative - adopt secondary value. Tier 3 (low): sources uninformative - set specialty default. Two audit columns appended: one recording source used one recording confidence tier.

title: Three-tier specialty reconciliation with audit columns — mysterycall_reconcile_specialty
text: data data frame. primary_col Character scalar. Column containing broad specialty label registry source NPPES DAC (e.g. "Otolaryngology - Head & Neck Surgery"). use column carry subspecialty values; subspecialty must come via secondary_col board certification data . secondary_col Optional character scalar. Column containing subspecialty label derived exclusively board certification data (e.g. ABOHNS certification_type parsed mysterycall_parse_certification_subspecialty()). DAC NPPES columns must passed subspecialty purposes. default Character scalar. "uninformative" label triggers tier-2 tier-3 logic. Default "General". source_col Character scalar. Name new audit column recording source used. Default "specialty_source". confidence_col Character scalar. Name new audit column recording tier ("high", "medium", "low"). Default "specialty_confidence".

Labels result "significant" p < alpha_screen.

title: Search NPI Database by Taxonomy — mysterycall_search_taxonomy
text: function returns curated subset npi::npi_flatten() output. Retained (renaming): npi, first_name, last_name, middle_name, credential, addresses_city, addresses_state, addresses_postal_code, addresses_telephone_number, addresses_country_name, taxonomies_desc, taxonomies_primary, search_term. columns returned npi_flatten() explicit drop list also retained. Always dropped regardless NPI API returns: endpoints_* fields (electronic health endpoint metadata) other_names_* fields (former alternate name records) identifiers_* fields (legacy identifier records) Supplementary address fields: addresses_address_2, addresses_fax_number, addresses_address_type, addresses_country_code Basic metadata: basic_last_updated, basic_status, basic_name_prefix, basic_name_suffix, basic_certification_date Secondary taxonomy fields: taxonomies_code, taxonomies_taxonomy_group, taxonomies_state, taxonomies_license Internal working column: credential_lower access dropped columns, call npi::npi_search() npi::npi_flatten() directly filtering.

title: Search NPI Database by Taxonomy — mysterycall_search_taxonomy
text: Inputs: taxonomy_to_search must exact NUCC taxonomy description string (see mysterycall::taxonomy dataset valid values). NPI registry API must reachable; function retries 3 times exponential back-returning empty data frame. Guarantees: Returns zero-row data frame (never NULL) records found. Output rows deduplicated NPI. write_snapshot = TRUE, .rds file written output_dir reproducible re-runs without re-querying live API. Fails : Network unavailable retries (returns empty data frame, error). states contains invalid two-letter abbreviation (silently skipped).

title: Search NPI Database by Taxonomy — mysterycall_search_taxonomy
text: O(t * p / 200) HTTP requests t = number state batches p = max_records (default 1,200). page request targets < 200 rows. Full national search across 50 states one taxonomy takes ~2-5 min depending registry load. Results cached -memory per session use_cache = TRUE.

Model 2: adjusted (insurance + practice setting) m2 <- structure(   list(     or_table = data.frame(       term        = c("(Intercept)", "insuranceMedicaid", "settingAcademic"),       or          = c(3.20, 0.65, 1.18),       ci_lower    = c(1.80, 0.42, 0.79),       ci_upper    = c(5.70, 1.01, 1.77),       p_value     = c(0.0003, 0.055, 0.417),       p_value_fmt = c("< 0.001", "0.055", "0.417"),       stringsAsFactors = FALSE     ),     n   = 160L,     aic = 208.1   ),   class = "mysterycall_logistic_model" )  # Model 3: adjusted + insurance x setting interaction m3 <- structure(   list(     or_table = data.frame(       term        = c("(Intercept)", "insuranceMedicaid",                       "settingAcademic",                       "insuranceMedicaid:settingAcademic"),       or          = c(3.10, 0.68, 1.21, 0.85),       ci_lower    = c(1.70, 0.43, 0.80, 0.51),       ci_upper    = c(5.60, 1.07, 1.84, 1.42),       p_value     = c(0.0005, 0.094, 0.371, 0.530),       p_value_fmt = c("< 0.001", "0.094", "0.371", "0.530"),       stringsAsFactors = FALSE     ),     n   = 160L,     aic = 209.7   ),   class = "mysterycall_logistic_model" )  tbl <- mysterycall_sensitivity_table(   models        = list("Unadjusted" = m1,                        "Adjusted"   = m2,                        "+ Interaction" = m3),   exposure_term = "insuranceMedicaid",   digits        = 2L ) print(tbl) #>           Characteristic                   Unadjusted #> 1 insuranceMedicaid (OR) 0.62 (0.40 to 0.97), p=0.036 #> 2            Sample size                        N=160 #> 3                    AIC                        210.4 #>                       Adjusted                + Interaction #> 1 0.65 (0.42 to 1.01), p=0.055 0.68 (0.43 to 1.07), p=0.094 #> 2                        N=160                        N=160 #> 3                        208.1                        209.7  # ---- Mixed model types: logistic + Poisson side by side ------------------- m_poisson <- structure(   list(     irr_table = data.frame(       term        = c("(Intercept)", "insuranceMedicaid"),       irr         = c(18.3, 1.41),       ci_lower    = c(14.1, 1.08),       ci_upper    = c(23.7, 1.84),       p_value     = c(0.0001, 0.012),       p_value_fmt = c("< 0.001", "0.012"),       stringsAsFactors = FALSE     ),     n   = 145L,     aic = 893.6   ),   class = "mysterycall_poisson_model" )  tbl2 <- mysterycall_sensitivity_table(   models        = list("Offered appt (OR)" = m2,                        "Wait days (IRR)"   = m_poisson),   exposure_term = "insuranceMedicaid",   digits        = 2L ) print(tbl2) #>      Characteristic            Offered appt (OR)              Wait days (IRR) #> 1 insuranceMedicaid 0.65 (0.42 to 1.01), p=0.055 1.41 (1.08 to 1.84), p=0.012 #> 2       Sample size                        N=160                        N=145 #> 3               AIC                        208.1                        893.6

title: Simple Poisson Regression for Group Comparison of Count Outcomes — mysterycall_simple_poisson
code: set.seed(1) df <- data.frame(   days      = rpois(120, lambda = 12),   insurance = rep(c("BCBS", "Medicaid", "Medicare"), 40) ) result <- mysterycall_simple_poisson(df, "days", "insurance",                                      reference = "BCBS",                                      outcome_label = "business days until appointment") #> Fitting simple Poisson GLM: days ~ insurance cat(result$summary_statement) #> Simple Poisson regression was used in place of Kruskal-Wallis because business days until appointment is a count outcome (non-negative integers). Poisson regression models the incidence rate ratio (IRR) directly, which is more interpretable than a rank-based test statistic for count data. The baseline rate (BCBS) is estimated at 11.93 events. For Medicaid compared to BCBS, the business days until appointment rate is approximately 1.03 times higher (2.7% higher; 95% CI: 0.91 to 1.17, p 0.676). For Medicare compared to BCBS, the business days until appointment rate is approximately 1.03 times higher (2.9% higher; 95% CI: 0.91 to 1.17, p 0.653). print(result$irr_table) #>                term    level      irr  ci_lower ci_upper   p_value p_value_fmt #> 1 insuranceMedicaid Medicaid 1.027254 0.9055750 1.165365 0.6759184       0.676 #> 2 insuranceMedicare Medicare 1.029350 0.9074831 1.167672 0.6527383       0.653 #>   direction #> 1    higher #> 2    higher

title: Association Test for a Contingency Table (auto chi-squared / Fisher) — mysterycall_test_categorical
text: data data frame. row_var, col_var Character scalars. Names two categorical columns cross-tabulate. method Character. "auto" (default) uses exact test expected count < min_expected, otherwise chi-squared; "chisq" "fisher" force choice. tables larger 2x2 exact test Fisher-Freeman-Halton test (simulated exact computation infeasible). min_expected Numeric. Expected-count threshold triggers exact test "auto". Default 5. correct Logical. Apply Yates' continuity correction 2x2 chi-squared tests. Default TRUE. posthoc Logical. TRUE outcome binary overall test significant 1 - conf_level, compute pairwise proportion comparisons across variable's levels. Default FALSE. p_adjust Character. Multiple-comparison method post-hoc p-values, passed stats::p.adjust(). Default "BH". conf_level Numeric. Confidence level (drives post-hoc alpha). Default 0.95.

title: Compute the wait-time equalization (crossover) point between two insurance groups — mysterycall_wait_time_crossover
text: Beyond crossover point, group1 patients experience longer waits group2 patients (\(0 < m < 1\) crossover exists). Crossover formula. regression line \(y = m x + b\).  Setting \(y = x\) (45-degree line) solving gives \(x = b / (1 - m)\).  finite, positive crossover requires \(0 < m < 1\): \(m \ge 1\): regression line never crosses y = x; group2 wait times diverge group1. \(m \le 0\): relationship non-positive; meaningful equalization point exists. log_transform = TRUE regression operates \(\log(\text{days})\); crossover solved log scale returned \(\exp(x_{\text{cross}})\). Pairing. Observations matched id_col using merge(..., = id_col, = FALSE), physicians appearing insurance groups contribute.  physician one observation per group, observations kept merged natural order subsetting; studies exactly one call per physician per group unambiguous.

title: Scrape ABOG Physicians via Tor (privacy-first) — scrape_physicians_data_with_tor
text: startID Integer. First diplomate ID query. endID Integer. Last diplomate ID query (inclusive). tor_ports Integer vector Tor SOCKS5 proxy ports (default 9050).  Supply multiple ports – e.g. c(9050, 9052, 9054, 9056) – enable parallel scraping: ID range split length(tor_ports) chunks chunk scraped forked process different Tor circuit.  Requires tor daemon configured one SocksPort per entry (see /opt/homebrew/etc/tor/torrc).  Use 9150 Tor Browser (single port ). tor_control_port Integer. Tor control port circuit rotation (default 9051).  Pass NULL disable rotation entirely. tor_control_password Character. Control-port password (default "", .e. password – typical localhost-setups). skip_ids_paths Optional character vector paths CSV Parquet files containing IDs skip.  file may column named WrongIDs, UnknownIDs, FailedIDs – recognised automatically.  Pass UnknownIDs_*.csv /FailedIDs_*.csv files previous run avoid re-querying IDs already confirmed empty persistently failed. output_format "csv" (default) "parquet". output_dir Directory output files. Created absent. Defaults tempdir(). checkpoint_every Save partial results every N successful records (default 100). Set Inf disable. max_retries Maximum retry attempts per ID transient errors (default 3). sleep_min Minimum seconds requests (default 2).  Increase conservative. sleep_max Maximum seconds requests (default 5). rotate_tor_every Request new Tor circuit every N requests (default 25). Lower values mean exit-node diversity cost slightly delay (2 s per rotation).  Set Inf disable. descending Logical. TRUE, iterate endID startID recently issued (highest-numbered) IDs scraped first (default FALSE).  Combine find_max_abog_id always start current top registry. max_skip_age_days Integer. Maximum age (days) "confirmed empty" record ID re-queried (default 180 – six months).  Files ConfirmedEmptyAt column use per-row timestamps; older files without column judged file modification date.  Set Inf trust skip files forever (recommended – newly certified physicians can fill previously empty IDs). verbose Logical. Print per-ID progress (default TRUE). torPort Integer. Tor SOCKS5 proxy port.  Use 9150 (default) Tor Browser 9050 tor daemon.

title: Scrape ABOG Physicians via Tor (privacy-first) — scrape_physicians_data_with_tor
text: data frame scraped physician records columns ABOG JSON response plus ID ScrapedAt.

title: Scrape ABOG Physicians via Tor (privacy-first) — scrape_physicians_data_with_tor
text: Privacy protections (order importance): Tor verification – confirms Tor exit node use scraping begins; aborts check fails. Circuit rotation – requests new Tor exit node every rotate_tor_every requests, limiting much traffic single exit node sees. Randomised timing – request waits random interval [sleep_min, sleep_max] seconds, traffic fingerprinted fixed inter-request cadence. Randomised User-Agent – request picks different browser string repeated requests look like different clients. Transient-error retry – 429 / 5xx network errors retried exponential back-; confirmed 404 / empty responses logged genuinely found.  prevents valid records silently lost. Checkpoint saves – results written disk every checkpoint_every records data lost session interrupted.

Keyed ZCTA (corresponds closely mailing ZIP), joins physician's practice ZIP directly, without tract crosswalk.

title: Social Vulnerability Index (SVI) by ZCTA — svi_zcta
text: data frame 33,800 rows 7 columns: zcta Five-digit ZIP Code Tabulation Area, character string (leading zeros preserved). svi Overall SVI percentile rank (CDC RPL_themes), 0-1; higher = vulnerable. svi_socioeconomic Theme 1 – Socioeconomic Status percentile rank (CDC RPL_theme1). svi_household Theme 2 – Household Characteristics percentile rank (CDC RPL_theme2). svi_minority Theme 3 – Racial Ethnic Minority Status percentile rank (CDC RPL_theme3). svi_housing_transport Theme 4 – Housing Type Transportation percentile rank (CDC RPL_theme4). year ACS 5-year vintage end year (2022 = 2018-2022).

title: Social Vulnerability Index (SVI) by ZCTA — svi_zcta
text: American Community Survey 5-year estimates (US Census Bureau), summarised CDC/ATSDR Social Vulnerability Index methodology implemented findSVI. See https://www.atsdr.cdc.gov/placeandhealth/svi/ reference methodology.

title: Social Vulnerability Index (SVI) by ZCTA — svi_zcta
text: Values national percentile ranks [0, 1]; higher = socially vulnerable. overall index (svi) rank sum four theme ranks. 2% ZCTAs NA (ACS input suppressed zero population). Regenerate data-raw/svi_zcta.R (requires Census API key CENSUS_API_KEY). Ranks national; findSVI recomputes ACS rather downloading CDC release, small differences official CDC ZCTA tables possible, chiefly suppressed low-population areas.

text: Matched-pair within-practice analyses, generalized labubu mystery-caller study (hand-rolled ). matched-pair design – practice called two scenarios (insurance types, caller personas) – package’s core paradigm, package previously offered unmatched GLMM; add matched comparison removes practice’s baseline generosity: mysterycall_paired_acceptance_mcnemar(): exact McNemar test binary acceptance outcome pairwise scenario contrast – discordant split, odds ratio, exact p-value, minimum detectable odds ratio chosen power (effective n discordant count, since discordant practices carry information). mysterycall_paired_wait_within_practice(): continuous analogue – pairs practices called scenarios, reports mean within-practice wait difference paired-t CI, paired t-test Wilcoxon signed-rank p-values, minimum detectable difference days. Closes footgun – model fitters require random_intercept column package previously gave nothing build one, blank/NA keys silently collapse one giant cluster corrupt random-effect variance. mysterycall_cumulative_access_curve(): empirical cumulative proportion calls secured appointment business-day t – correct primitive single-contact design, mysterycall_kaplan_meier()’s right-censoring non-offered calls implies follow-design . curve plateaus share obtained within horizon (offer rate every wait falls inside ). Optional step-curve figure. mysterycall_twopart_power(): Monte Carlo power two-part outcome (offer Bernoulli full sample; wait negative binomial offered subset) access audits universally – reports power part separately, since single-outcome calculator understates wait model’s sample (runs offered subset). Depends MASS. mysterycall_marginal_power(): Monte Carlo power post-stratification-weighted, population-marginal effect paired-call design (subject called two conditions; stratum oversampled sample reweighted target population mix). Reports power conditional interaction, unweighted marginal effect, population-weighted marginal effect. Needs glmmTMB + marginaleffects. mysterycall_type_i_check() mysterycall_find_mde(): generic companions simulation power function – null-calibration self-check (observed type rate + exact binomial CI + verdict) minimum-detectable-effect binary search user-supplied power function.
